correctness.rationale: Under the exact bijection from half-graph edges to pairs of an ordered (n+1)-set, every image triangle is the image of three consecutive edges of a length-three geodesic. Mantel therefore gives the sharp upper bound. Balanced complete bipartite images are feasible exactly when their ordered two-coloring has at most three runs; four runs produce an explicit forbidden geodesic triple. The equality case of Mantel proves that these are all maxima. Direct counting of two- and three-run balanced strings proves the optimizer count. A definition-level checker corroborates all near-extremal cases through n=6.

value.rationale: Half graphs are the canonical twin-free chain graphs and edge general position is a natural geodesic extremal invariant. The result reveals an exact correspondence with Mantel extremality: the maximum value is quadratic, every optimizer is a balanced complete bipartition with an ordered three-run restriction, and the exact number of optimizers follows. This is structural extremal information rather than a routine parameter substitution.
